Theme

Latin word

quisquis

quisquis, quicquid (quidquid)

relative pronoun, with a verb of its own

whatever, whoever; whoever

In this lexicon

  • whatever

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.2.14: quidquid dēlīrant rēgēs, plectuntur Achīvī; Cic. Att. 12.1.2: garrīmus quicquid in buccam; Traupman 406

  • whoever

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Amph. 309b: Quisquis homō hūc profectō vēnerit, pugnōs edet.; Sen. Ep. 20.13: quisquis exit in lūcem

Examples

  • quārē habē tibi quidquid hoc libellī quālecumque

    so take this little book for your own, whatever it is, such as it isCatull. 1.8–9

    In the entry for whatever

  • quidquid dēlīrant rēgēs, plectuntur Achīvī

    whatever madness the kings commit, the Greeks pay for itHor. Ep. 1.2.14

    In the entry for whatever

  • quidquid est, ubicumque est, quodcumque agit, renīdet

    whatever it is, wherever he is, whatever he is doing, he grinsCatull. 39.6–7

    whatever you teach, be brief, so that minds may grasp what is said quickly, learn it and keep it faithfullyHor. AP 335–336
